tasks.g4m_md_q4: Tali’s expedition walked 25 600 steps in a week. The explorer wrote this number in the diary. How do you read it correctly?
tasks.g4m_md2_q1: Tali is entering the safe code: the number 6 253. He says: “The digit 2 here is 2 thousand!” The safe won’t open. What does the digit 2 really mean in 6 253?
tasks.g4m_md2_q2: Digit broke the number 9 070 into place-value parts for Tali. Which way is correct?
tasks.g4m_md2_q3: In the number 4 816 Tali is looking for the digit 8. “It’s in the thousands place — the most important!” he decided. Correct Tali: in which place is the 8?
tasks.g4m_md2_q4: Cipher master Tali coded a number: “5 thousands, 0 hundreds, 3 tens, 9 ones.” Now it needs decoding. What number is it?
tasks.g4m_md3_q1: Tali looks at two treasures: 8 450 and 8 540 coins. He says: “They’re the same — both start with an eight!” Tali is rushing and isn’t looking carefully. Which treasure is actually bigger?
tasks.g4m_md3_q2: Digit asks to put the numbers in order — from smallest to largest: 3 099, 3 900, and 3 009. Tali tries, but gets lost in the zeros. Help him!
tasks.g4m_md3_q3: Tali wrote in his diary: “5 008 > 5 080 — that’s true, because in the first number the eight stands near the start!” Is his reasoning correct?
tasks.g4m_md3_q4: Two trains race for the longer route: the first traveled 12 375 km, the second — 12 735 km. Tali cheers for the second. Is he right — did the second really go farther?

tasks.g4m_md3_q4_b: Yes, the second train went farther

intro.jungleAdd_0_body: When we add, we join two numbers. For example: 2 bananas and 3 bananas make 5 bananas!
intro.jungleAdd_1_body: Show 2 fingers, then raise 3 more. Count them all: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5! That's addition!
intro.jungleSub_0_body: When we subtract, we take part away. Had 5 bananas, ate 2 — now there are 3 left!
intro.jungleSub_1_body: You can subtract by counting backwards! 5... 4... 3. Took away 2 — got 3. Try it yourself!
intro.jungleCmp_0_body: Which number is BIGGER? 7 and 4 — 7 is bigger than 4! The sign > means 'greater than'. 7 > 4.
intro.jungleCmp_1_body: Imagine a crocodile: its mouth always opens towards the BIGGER number! 7 > 4 — the croc faces 7. It wants to eat more!
intro.canyonWords_0_body: Every word is made of letters together. D + O + G = DOG. S + U + N = SUN. We read letter by letter!
intro.canyonWords_1_body: Look at the whole word and say it. 'dog' = dog, 'sun' = sun, 'red' = red. Keep practising and you'll remember!
intro.canyonSent_0_body: Words together make a sentence! 'The big dog runs.' Look for the main character — who is the sentence about?
intro.canyonSent_1_body: When reading, ask yourself: Who? What kind? What does it do? This helps you understand the meaning!
intro.labAnimals_0_body: There are millions of animals on Earth! Some live in water, some fly in the sky, and others walk on land.
intro.labAnimals_1_body: Scientists ask: Where does it live? What does it eat? How many legs? Can it fly? Let's be scientists too!
intro.labPhysics_0_body: When both sides of a scale have the same weight, they stay level. This is called BALANCE!
intro.labPhysics_1_body: If one side is heavier, the scale tips that way. Add weight — the balance changes. Try it!
intro.spacePlanets_0_body: Our Solar System has 8 planets. They all orbit around the Sun on their own paths!
intro.spacePlanets_1_body: We live on planet Earth — the third planet from the Sun. It has water, air, and life. That makes it special!
intro.spaceSolar_0_title: The Sun is at the centre!
intro.spaceSolar_0_body: The Solar System = the Sun + 8 planets + asteroids and comets. Everything orbits around the Sun!
intro.spaceSolar_1_body: From the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune. There are 8 — remember them!
intro.meadow_c5l1_0_b: Numbers help us count: how many apples, how many steps, how many toys! Let's start with 1, 2, and 3!
intro.meadow_c5l1_1_b: Raise 1 finger — that's one! Raise another — two! One more — three! Try it yourself!
intro.meadow_c5l2_0_b: After three comes four, and after four comes five! One hand has exactly 5 fingers!
intro.meadow_c5l2_1_b: Show all 5 fingers on one hand. See? That's the number 5! 4 + 1 = 5.
intro.meadow_c5l3_0_b: Which pile is MORE? Where there are more berries, that number is BIGGER! 4 > 2.
intro.meadow_c5l3_1_b: Draw as many dots as the number says. Where there are more dots — that number is BIGGER!
intro.meadow_c10l1_0_b: After five come six and seven! Count 6 berries: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6!
intro.meadow_c10l1_1_b: Show 5 fingers on one hand, then 2 fingers on the other. That makes seven!
intro.meadow_c10l2_0_b: 8 = 5 + 3. 9 = 5 + 4. Count on the fingers of both hands!
intro.meadow_c10l2_1_b: 10 = 5 + 5 = all fingers on both hands! Nine is the biggest single-digit number; ten uses two digits!
intro.meadow_c10l3_0_b: 7 is more than 3, 9 is more than 6! The farther from 1, the BIGGER the number!
intro.meadow_shl1_0_b: A circle is a round shape with no corners! A ball, a coin, the sun — all look like circles!
intro.meadow_shl1_1_b: A square has 4 sides and 4 corners, all sides are EQUAL! Find a square object nearby!
intro.meadow_shl2_0_b: A triangle has 3 corners and 3 sides. A house roof is a triangle!
intro.meadow_shl2_1_b: A rectangle is like a square but with different side lengths! Books, doors — all rectangles!
intro.meadow_shl3_0_b: Look around: a window is a rectangle, a plate is a circle! Shapes are everywhere!
intro.meadow_shl3_1_b: Square (4 corners), Rectangle (4 corners), Triangle (3), Circle (0 corners) — well done!
intro.forest_vl1_0_b: The Russian alphabet has 33 letters. А is a vowel, you can sing it: АААА! Words: Арбуз (watermelon), Аист (stork)!
intro.forest_vl1_1_b: Vowels — А, О, У, И, Э and more — you can hold the sound! АААА!
intro.forest_vl2_0_b: О-О-О! The mouth opens like a small circle. Words with О: Овощи (vegetables), Облако (cloud)!
intro.forest_vl2_1_t: Letter У — lips like a tube!
intro.forest_vl2_1_b: У-У-У! Lips form a tube shape. Words with У: Утка (duck), Улитка (snail)!
intro.forest_vl3_0_b: И-И-И! Smile wide! Words: Игрушка (toy), Игла (needle). Э-Э-Э! Words: Эхо (echo)!
intro.forest_vl3_1_b: А, О, У, И, Э — 5 vowels you know! In АИСТ there are А and И — two vowels!
intro.forest_conl1_0_b: М-М-М... Mouth closed, sound through nose! М is a consonant. Words: Мама (mama), Мяч (ball)!
intro.forest_conl1_1_b: С-С-С... Like a hissing snake! С is a consonant. Words: Солнце (sun), Собака (dog)!
intro.forest_conl2_0_b: Т-Т-Т! Tongue touches upper teeth. Words: Тигр (tiger), Тарелка (plate)!
intro.forest_conl2_1_b: К-К-К! Like a frog croaking! Words: Кот (cat), Книга (book)!
intro.forest_conl3_0_b: Н-Н-Н! Sound through nose. Words: Нос (nose), Небо (sky), Нора (burrow)!
intro.forest_conl3_1_b: М, С, Т, К, Н — 5 consonants! МА = М + А! Put letters together to make syllables!
intro.forest_syll1_0_t: A syllable is a piece of a word!
intro.forest_syll1_0_b: A syllable is a consonant + vowel! МА, МО, МУ are syllables! МАМА = МА + МА = 2 syllables!
intro.forest_syll1_1_b: МА! Start with М and immediately say А. МО — same: М + О!
intro.forest_syll2_0_b: С + А = СА! С + О = СО! С + У = СУ! Word СОВА (owl) = СО + ВА = 2 syllables!
intro.forest_syll2_1_b: Clap СОВА: СО-ВА — two claps! МАМА — МА-МА — two claps!
intro.forest_syll3_0_b: НА = Н + А! Word НОРА (burrow) = НО + РА = 2 syllables. Clap: НО-РА!
intro.forest_syll3_1_b: МА, МО, МУ, СА, СО, СУ, НА — syllables! Build words: МА-МА, НО-РА!
intro.garden_coll1_0_b: There are many colors! Basic ones: Red, Blue, Green. All other colors come from these!
intro.garden_coll1_1_b: Red apple, blue sky, green grass. Name the colors you see!
intro.garden_coll2_0_b: Yellow — like the sun and banana! Orange — like an orange and carrot!
intro.garden_coll2_1_b: Elephant is BIG, ant is SMALL. A whale is big, a mouse is small!
intro.garden_coll3_0_b: White — like snow and milk. Black — like the night sky!
intro.garden_coll3_1_b: Red + Blue = Purple! Blue + Yellow = Green! Artists mix paints!
intro.garden_animl1_0_b: Domestic animals live with people: cow, horse, cat, dog, chicken!
intro.garden_animl1_1_b: Cow gives milk, chicken gives eggs, dog guards the home, cat catches mice!
intro.garden_animl2_0_b: Wild animals live in nature — forests, steppes, mountains! Wolf, bear, fox are wild!
intro.garden_animl2_1_b: In the forest live: bear, wolf, fox, hare. We observe them from a distance!
intro.garden_animl3_0_b: Fish live in water, birds fly in the sky. Fish have gills, birds have wings!
intro.garden_animl3_1_b: A cat has 4 legs, a bird has 2 legs. Cats run on four legs!
intro.garden_seasl1_0_b: In autumn leaves turn yellow and fall, it gets colder. Birds fly south!
intro.garden_seasl1_1_b: In winter everything is white with snow! Rivers freeze. Children build snowmen!
intro.garden_seasl2_0_b: In spring snow melts, first flowers bloom, birds return, trees get leaves!
intro.garden_seasl2_1_b: Spring is the start of nature's new year! After winter everything comes alive!
intro.garden_seasl3_0_b: In summer everything grows: vegetables, fruits, berries. Days are long and warm!
intro.garden_seasl3_1_b: Winter → Spring → Summer → Autumn → Winter →... They repeat every year!
intro.island_abcl1_0_b: English has 26 letters! We start with A like Apple and B like Ball!
intro.island_abcl1_1_t: A is for Apple, B is for Ball!
intro.island_abcl1_1_b: A — apple, ant! B — ball, banana! Say the letters out loud: A! B!
intro.island_abcl2_0_b: C — cat, coconut, cloud! D — dog, dolphin, door! Listen to the sounds!
intro.island_abcl2_1_b: Say: C-C-C like Cat! D-D-D like Dog! Can you think of more words?
intro.island_abcl3_0_b: E — egg, elephant, ear! F — frog, fish, flower! Great progress!
intro.island_abcl3_1_b: You know A, B, C, D, E, F! That's 6 letters! Keep going, you're doing great!
intro.island_coll1_0_b: Red, Blue, Green — say them out loud!
intro.island_coll1_1_b: What is RED? Apple! What is BLUE? Sky! What is GREEN? Grass! Name them!
intro.island_coll2_0_b: Yellow — sun, banana! Orange — orange fruit, carrot!
intro.island_coll2_1_b: Say: YELLOW like the sun! ORANGE like the fruit! Listen and repeat!
intro.island_coll3_0_b: White — snow! Black — night! Green — frog!
intro.island_coll3_1_b: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, White, Black — you know 7 colors in English!
intro.island_animl1_0_b: Cat, Dog — these are our pets! Say: CAT! DOG!
intro.island_animl1_1_b: Cat says MEOW, Dog says WOOF! Try making the sounds!
intro.island_animl2_0_b: Bird — flies in the sky! Fish — swims in water!
intro.island_animl2_1_b: Bird → sky, Fish → water, Cat → home! Match them!
intro.island_animl3_0_b: Cow says MOO! We learned: cat, dog, bird, fish, cow — 5 animals!
intro.island_animl3_1_b: Cat, Dog, Bird, Fish, Cow — 5 animal words! Plus Red, Blue, Green, Yellow — 4 colors! Amazing!
intro.g3m_divl2_1_b: Remainder = dividend − quotient × divisor. It's always less than the divisor.
intro.g3m_divl3_0_b: Big numbers — use long division, step by step.
intro.g3e_dailyl1_0_b: Everyone has a daily routine. In English it is called daily routine.
intro.g3e_dailyl1_1_b: Use: wake up, eat, go to school, play, sleep — to describe your day.
intro.g3e_dailyl2_0_b: What time is it? It is... o'clock — ...саат.
intro.g3e_dailyl2_1_b: in the morning = таңда, in the afternoon = түштө, in the evening = кечинде.
intro.g3e_dailyl3_0_b: I wake up at 7. I eat breakfast. I go to school.
intro.g3e_dailyl3_1_b: Connect with: then, after that, finally.
intro.g1m_c20l1_0_b: After 10 come 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. Keep counting from ten!
intro.g1m_c20l1_1_b: Which number is bigger: 12 or 15? 15 is bigger!
intro.g1m_c20l2_0_b: 16, 17, 18, 19, 20 — the last numbers of the second ten!
intro.g1m_c20l2_1_b: Which number is between 16 and 18? That's right — 17!
intro.g1m_c20l3_0_b: 14 and 17 — which is smaller? 14 is less than 17!
intro.g1m_c20l3_1_b: 20 and 20 — they are equal! The = sign means 'equals'.
intro.g1m_addl1_0_b: 3 + 4 = 7. Count on your fingers or in your head!
intro.g1m_subl1_1_b: Addition and subtraction are opposite operations!
intro.g1r_vowl1_0_b: Vowels can be sung! In the word UTKA the first letter is U!
intro.g1r_vowl1_1_b: Я, Ю, Е, Ё make consonants soft. КONЬ has a soft Н!
intro.g1r_vowl2_0_b: In the word ЮЛА the first letter is Ю. In ЕЛЬ the first is Е!
intro.g1r_vowl2_1_b: А is hard, Я is soft. Mama — Maya!
intro.g1r_vowl3_0_b: КОН is hard, КОНЬ is soft. Ь shows softness!
intro.g1r_vowl3_1_b: А, О, У, И, Э, Я, Ю, Е, Ё — 10 vowel letters!
intro.g1r_wrdl1_0_b: К-О-Т — КОТ. Read syllable by syllable!
intro.g1r_wrdl1_1_b: СОМ — one syllable. МА-МА — two syllables!
intro.g1r_wrdl2_0_b: СТОЛ and СТУЛ differ by just one letter! Read carefully!
intro.g1r_wrdl2_1_b: ТРА-ВА — two syllables. КНИ-ГА — two syllables!
intro.g1r_wrdl3_0_b: A sentence expresses a thought. It starts with a capital letter!
intro.g1r_wrdl3_1_b: At the end — a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark!
intro.g1r_grml1_0_b: Names, nicknames, start of a sentence — with a capital letter!
intro.g1r_grml1_1_b: Маша, Москва, Тали — written with a capital!
intro.g1r_grml2_0_b: Full stop — at the end. Question mark — in a question!
intro.g1r_grml2_1_b: Who is this? — question. Mum is home. — statement.
intro.g1r_grml3_0_b: WHO — about people and animals. WHAT — about objects!
intro.g1r_grml3_1_b: Who is running? What is growing? Who is singing?
intro.g1w_schl1_0_b: Pen, notebook, textbook, pencil case — what's in the bag!
intro.g1w_schl1_1_b: In the classroom — desks, a board, a teacher. A lesson lasts 45 minutes!
intro.g1w_schl2_1_b: In PE we run and jump. In art — we draw!
intro.g1w_schl3_0_t: School is a place of knowledge!
intro.g1w_schl3_0_b: At school we learn to read, count, and discover new things!
intro.g1w_schl3_1_b: Keep learning! Every day brings new discoveries!
intro.g1w_natl1_0_b: Oak, birch, spruce — they have a trunk, branches and leaves!
intro.g1w_natl1_1_b: Hare, fox, bear, birds — they live in the forest!
intro.g1w_natl2_0_b: The elephant lives in Africa. The cow is a domestic animal!
intro.g1w_natl2_1_b: Sun, rain, snow — the weather changes!
intro.g1w_natl3_0_b: In autumn leaves turn yellow. In winter — snow. In spring — flowers!
intro.g1w_natl3_1_b: Do not litter, do not break trees. We are part of nature!
intro.g1w_bdyl1_0_b: Eyes see, ears hear, nose smells, hands touch!
intro.g1w_bdyl1_1_b: Fruit is good for you! A banana is tasty and nutritious!
intro.g1w_bdyl2_0_b: Bones are a support. Muscles help us move!
intro.g1w_bdyl2_1_b: Sleep is when the body rests. Sleep 9–10 hours!
intro.g1w_bdyl3_0_b: Do not talk to strangers! Do not open the door to unfamiliar people!
intro.g1w_bdyl3_1_b: Cross on green! Look both ways!
intro.g1e_abcl1_0_b: G — goat, H — house. Learning English!
intro.g1e_abcl2_0_b: K — kitten, L — lion. Memorise them!
intro.g1e_abcl3_0_b: O — orange, P — parrot. Almost half the alphabet!
intro.g1e_abcl3_1_b: You know the letters up to R! There is more to come!
intro.g1e_numl1_0_b: One, two, three, four, five — count in English!
intro.g1e_numl2_1_b: Ten is the most important number!
intro.g1e_numl3_0_b: Two plus three = five! Count in English!
intro.g1e_grtl1_0_b: Hello! Hi! Good morning! — say hello!
intro.g1e_grtl1_1_b: Hello — when you meet someone. Good morning — in the morning!
intro.g1e_grtl2_0_b: I am a student. You are my friend!
intro.g1e_grtl2_1_b: My name is... What is your name?
intro.g1e_grtl3_0_b: Thank you and Please are two very important polite phrases!
intro.g1e_grtl3_1_b: Books — read books to learn new English words!
intro.g2m_100l1_0_b: Count in tens: 10, 20, 30… Like boxes of 10 — quicker!
intro.g2m_100l1_1_b: 100 is 10 × 10. That's a hundred — a key number!
intro.g2m_100l2_0_b: In a two-digit number: ones on the right, tens on the left. 25 = 2 tens and 5 ones.
intro.g2m_100l2_1_b: 47 = 40 + 7. Four tens and seven ones — that's 47!
intro.g2m_100l3_0_b: 99 is the largest two-digit number. Compare tens first, then ones.
intro.g2m_100l3_1_b: You can count to 100 and understand place value. Well done!
intro.g2m_add2l1_1_b: For two-digit numbers: add tens and ones separately, then combine.
intro.g2m_add2l2_0_b: 28 + 5: 28 + 2 = 30, then + 3 = 33. Reach a round ten first!
intro.g2m_timesl1_0_b: 2 × 3 means 3 twice: 3+3=6. Times 2 doubles the number.
intro.g2r_shl1_0_b: Л, Р, М before А, О, У are hard. ЛА, ЛО, ЛУ!
intro.g2r_shl1_1_b: ЛА is hard, ЛИ is soft. The letter shows it!
intro.g2r_shl2_0_b: Конь, соль, мать — Ь at the end makes the consonant soft!
intro.g2r_shl2_1_b: Ь does not represent a sound. Only softness!
intro.g2r_shl3_0_b: Любовь, лимон, лев — Л is soft before Я, Ю, Е!
intro.g2r_shl3_1_b: You know hard and soft consonants!
intro.g2r_spl1_0_b: A noun answers who? what? Table, mum, sun!
intro.g2r_spl1_1_b: A noun names an object or person!
intro.g2r_spl2_0_b: A verb answers what does it do? Runs, reads, sleeps!
intro.g2r_spl2_1_b: A verb is an action. The cat meows!
intro.g2r_spl3_0_b: Subject and predicate — the main members!
intro.g2r_spl3_1_b: Words in a sentence are connected by meaning!
intro.g2r_sentl1_0_b: Who? What? — subject. What does it do? — predicate!
intro.g2r_sentl1_1_b: Mum is cooking. Mum — subject, is cooking — predicate!
intro.g2r_sentl3_0_b: Words agree with each other in gender and number!
intro.g2r_sentl3_1_b: Red ball — masculine. Red rose — feminine!
intro.g2s_pltl1_0_b: Root, stem, leaves, flower — parts of a plant!
intro.g2s_pltl1_1_b: Root is in the soil. Leaves reach towards the sun!
intro.g2s_pltl2_0_b: A plant absorbs light and makes nutrients!
intro.g2s_pltl3_0_b: Carrot is a root vegetable. Apple is a fruit. Tomato is a vegetable!
intro.g2s_pltl3_1_b: Vegetables grow in the soil or in beds. Fruits — on trees!
intro.g2s_anil1_0_b: They feed their young with milk. Dog, cat, elephant!
intro.g2s_anil1_1_b: Mammals are warm-blooded and have fur!
intro.g2s_anil2_0_b: Feathers, beak, they fly! Sparrow, eagle, penguin!
intro.g2s_anil2_1_b: Birds lay eggs. Many can fly!
intro.g2s_anil3_0_b: Fish — in water, gills. Insects — 6 legs!
intro.g2s_anil3_1_b: Pike, carp — fish. Butterfly, ant — insects!
intro.g2s_bdyl1_0_b: Bones are support. Muscles help us move!
intro.g2s_bdyl1_1_b: Heart, lungs, stomach — inside the body!
intro.g2s_bdyl2_0_b: Vegetables, fruit, porridge — healthy! Sweets — in small amounts!
intro.g2s_bdyl2_1_b: Healthy eating is more important than sweets!
intro.g2s_bdyl3_0_b: Morning exercises, running, swimming — strengthen the body!
intro.g2s_bdyl3_1_b: Movement is life! Do physical exercise!
intro.g2e_daysl1_0_b: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday!
intro.g2e_daysl2_1_b: Today is Monday. Yesterday was Sunday!
intro.g2e_daysl3_0_b: What day is it today? On Monday we have math!
intro.g2e_phrl2_0_b: Excuse me — when you are in the way. Sorry — when you are at fault!
intro.g2e_phrl2_1_b: Excuse me — to get past. Sorry — if you step on someone's foot!
intro.g2e_phrl3_0_b: Can I? — Болобу? You can't — Болбойт!
intro.g2e_phrl3_1_b: Can I go? — Can I leave?
intro.g2e_schl1_0_b: Desk — парта, chair — отургуч, board — тактасы, book — китеп!
intro.g2e_schl3_0_b: May I come in? I do not understand. Can you help me?
intro.g2e_schl3_1_b: Can you help me? — Can you help me?
intro.g3m_1000l1_0_b: Hundreds: 100, 200… 1000 is a thousand. Three-digit numbers have a hundreds place.
intro.g3m_1000l1_1_b: Ones, tens, hundreds — each digit's value depends on its place!
intro.g3m_1000l2_0_b: 247 = 200 + 40 + 7. Two hundreds, four tens, seven ones.
intro.g3m_1000l3_0_b: 356 vs 298: hundreds first — 3 > 2, so 356 is greater.
intro.g3m_1000l3_1_b: Any three-digit beats a two-digit. Among three-digit, compare hundreds first.
intro.g3m_tabl1_0_b: 4 x 5 = 20, 6 x 7 = 42. Multiplying by 4 — double twice!
intro.g3m_tabl3_0_b: 9 x 5 = 45. The digits of any multiple of 9 always add up to 9!
intro.g3r_genl3_0_b: Big table, big book, big window!
intro.g3r_genl3_1_b: An adjective agrees with the noun!
intro.g3r_verbl1_0_b: I read, you read, he reads. Endings change by person!
intro.g3r_verbl1_1_b: 1st person: I, we. 2nd: you. 3rd: he, she, it, they!
intro.g3r_verbl2_0_b: Read (m.), read (f.), read (n.). Suffix -л and ending by gender!
intro.g3r_verbl2_1_b: I read (m.). She read (f.). It read (n.)!
intro.g3r_verbl3_0_b: 1st person: I go, we go. 2nd: you go. 3rd: he goes!
intro.g3r_verbl3_1_b: Endings change by person and number!
intro.g3r_adjl1_0_b: Red ball, red rose, red apple!
intro.g3r_adjl1_1_b: The adjective is in the same gender and number as the noun!
intro.g3r_adjl3_1_b: Antonyms are words with opposite meanings!
intro.g3w_geol1_0_b: North, south, east, west! A compass shows direction!
intro.g3w_geol1_1_b: A map is a flat representation of the Earth!
intro.g3w_geol2_0_b: A globe is a sphere. A map is flat!
intro.g3w_geol2_1_b: A globe is a small-scale model of the Earth!
intro.g3w_geol3_0_b: Russia — Moscow. France — Paris. Every country has a capital!
intro.g3w_geol3_1_b: A capital is the main city of a country!
intro.g3w_natl2_0_b: Oil, gas, coal — extracted from the ground!
intro.g3w_natl2_1_b: Natural resources are the riches of the Earth!
intro.g3w_natl3_0_b: Protect the forest, water, animals! We are part of nature!
intro.g3w_ecol1_0_b: A community of living organisms. Forest, meadow, pond!
intro.g3w_ecol2_0_b: Plant — hare — wolf! Who eats what!
intro.g3w_ecol2_1_b: Everyone is part of the chain!
intro.g3w_ecol3_0_b: We are part of the ecosystem! Our actions affect nature!
intro.g3e_tobel1_0_b: I am, you are, he/she/it is! Am with I, is with he/she/it!
intro.g3e_tobel1_1_b: I am happy. You are smart!
intro.g3e_tobel2_0_b: I am not, he is not, they are not. Not after am, is, are!
intro.g3e_tobel2_1_b: I'm not, he isn't, they aren't!
intro.g3e_tobel3_0_b: Am I? Is he? Are you? Am, is, are come first!
intro.g3e_tobel3_1_b: Are you ready? Yes, I am!
intro.g3e_foodl1_0_b: Apple, bread, milk, water. Food — тамак, drink — суусундук!
intro.g3e_foodl1_1_b: I like apples. I drink water!
intro.g3e_foodl2_0_t: I like / I do not like!
intro.g3e_foodl2_0_b: I like pizza. I don't like broccoli. I like it / I don't like it!
intro.g3e_foodl2_1_b: Do you like...? Yes, I do. No, I do not!
intro.g3e_foodl3_0_b: Can I have some water? Thank you! Table manners!
intro.g3e_foodl3_1_b: Please. Thank you. You are welcome!
intro.g3e_routel1_0_b: I get up. I brush my teeth. I go to school!
intro.g3e_routel1_1_b: Wake up — ойгонуу. Go to bed — уктоого баруу!
intro.g3e_routel2_0_b: What time is it? It's 7 o'clock! Half past — жарым!
intro.g3e_routel2_1_b: O'clock — for a full hour. 7:30 — half past seven!
intro.g3e_routel3_1_b: I always brush my teeth. I never skip breakfast!

dialog.jungle_add_1_0: Welcome to the Jungle of Numbers! I'm Tali, your dino buddy!
dialog.jungle_add_1_1: ROAR! Hi! I'm Rex! Please help me count my bananas!
dialog.jungle_add_2_0: Rex wants to share fruits with his friends! Let's add them up!
dialog.jungle_add_2_1: I found more mangoes! How many do I have now?
dialog.jungle_sub_1_0: Great job counting! Now let's learn subtraction!
dialog.jungle_sub_1_1: I had some bananas but I ate a few… How many are left?
dialog.jungle_sub_2_0: Rex is getting better at math! Let's try harder problems!
dialog.jungle_sub_2_1: My friends took some fruit. How many do I have left?
dialog.jungle_compare_1_0: Rex found two piles of rocks. Let's compare them!
dialog.jungle_compare_1_1: Which pile has MORE rocks? I cannot decide!
dialog.canyon_words_1_0: Welcome to Word Canyon! Dippy the dinosaur lives here!
dialog.canyon_words_1_1: Hello! I found ancient cave paintings. Help me read them!
dialog.canyon_words_2_0: Dippy received a letter from a faraway friend!
dialog.canyon_words_2_1: Can you help me read these words? I am still learning!
dialog.canyon_sent_1_0: Now let's read whole sentences! Dippy has a canyon map!
dialog.canyon_sent_1_1: The map has directions written on it. Can you read them?
dialog.lab_animals_1_0: Welcome to Spike's Science Lab! The ancient volcano is active!
dialog.lab_animals_1_1: GREETINGS! I am Spike! I study animals. Let us learn together!
dialog.lab_animals_2_0: Spike has more fascinating animals to show us!
dialog.lab_animals_2_1: My collection keeps growing! Can you identify them?
dialog.lab_physics_1_0: Now Spike wants to do a balance experiment!
dialog.lab_physics_1_1: Science is amazing! Watch what happens when we add weight!
dialog.space_planets_1_0: We made it to Space Valley! Look at all the stars!
dialog.space_planets_1_1: Screech! I am Stela! I fly between planets! Want to learn?
dialog.space_planets_2_0: Stela wants to show us more planets in the solar system!
dialog.space_planets_2_1: Each planet is unique! Let me show you!
dialog.space_solar_1_0: Let's explore the whole solar system with Stela!
dialog.space_solar_1_1: The universe is HUGE! Let me show you something amazing!
dialog.meadow_c5l1_0: Hi! I'm Bunny Zoya! Let's learn to count together!
dialog.meadow_c5l1_1: Hi! I'm Tali! Numbers help us count everything around us!
dialog.meadow_c5l2_0: Four carrots or five? I'm confused! Help me!
dialog.meadow_c5l2_1: Four is more than three, and five is more than four! Let's figure it out!
dialog.meadow_c5l3_0: Great job! Now let's talk — which is more? You can do it!
dialog.meadow_c5l3_1: I want more carrots! Help me pick the bigger pile!
dialog.meadow_c10l1_0: Six berries! Seven chicks! Let's keep counting!
dialog.meadow_c10l1_1: After 5 come 6 and 7. Let's keep counting!
dialog.meadow_c10l2_0: Eight, nine, ten — we're almost there!
dialog.meadow_c10l2_1: Nine is the biggest single-digit number! Ten uses two digits. Remember it!
dialog.meadow_c10l3_0: Show me: is 7 more than 3? You definitely know this!
dialog.meadow_c10l3_1: I'll collect more berries than you! Want to check?
dialog.meadow_shl1_0: Look — round and square things are all around us!
dialog.meadow_shl1_1: A circle rolls, a square stands still! They have different properties!
dialog.meadow_shl2_0: Three corners — that's a triangle! Look at the roof!
dialog.meadow_shl2_1: I found a rectangular leaf! It looks like a book!
dialog.meadow_shl3_0: Shapes are everywhere — at home, on the street, in nature!
dialog.meadow_shl3_1: Well done! You know all the basic geometric shapes!
dialog.forest_vl1_0: I found the letter А on the bark of a tree!
dialog.forest_vl1_1: The letter А is first in the alphabet and easy to sing: АААААА!
dialog.forest_vl2_0: Oh wow, letters О and У! They are vowels too!
dialog.forest_vl2_1: Vowel letters can be sung for a long time! О-О-О, У-У-У!
dialog.forest_vl3_0: Now let's learn И and Э! Almost all vowels will be yours!
dialog.forest_vl3_1: In the word АИСТ there are two vowels! Can you hear them?
dialog.forest_conl1_0: Look — the letter М! Мммм... You can't sing it for long!
dialog.forest_conl1_1: Consonant letters bump into something. М, С, Т, К, Н!
dialog.forest_conl2_0: Т-Т-Т! Tiger walks. К-К-К! Cat purrs!
dialog.forest_conl2_1: Letters Т and К are consonants. Hear how short they are!
dialog.forest_conl3_0: Letter Н — as in НОС (nose)! Also НЕБО, НОРА!
dialog.forest_conl3_1: I'm collecting letters in my backpack! Already five consonants!
dialog.forest_syll1_0: М + А = МА! That's what a syllable is! Hear it: МА-МА?
dialog.forest_syll1_1: A syllable is a piece of a word. МА-МА — two syllables!
dialog.forest_syll2_0: С + А = СА, С + О = СО! Сова (owl) is СО-ВА!
dialog.forest_syll2_1: I live in a burrow! Нора is НО-РА! Two syllables!
dialog.forest_syll3_0: The word НОРА is НО + РА. Two syllables!
dialog.forest_syll3_1: Excellent work! You can divide words into syllables!
dialog.garden_coll1_0: Welcome to my garden! I'm Tara! Look at all the colors!
dialog.garden_coll1_1: Colors help us describe everything around us!
dialog.garden_coll2_0: Yellow bananas, orange oranges — everything so bright!
dialog.garden_coll2_1: I'm small but smart! Turtles are very clever!
dialog.garden_coll3_0: We know so many colors! White snow, black night!
dialog.garden_coll3_1: Well done! Now you know all the basic colors!
dialog.garden_animl1_0: Domestic animals live in my garden! Let's meet them!
dialog.garden_animl1_1: Domestic animals live near people and help them!
dialog.garden_animl2_0: Wild animals live in forests and steppes! We don't go near them!
dialog.garden_animl2_1: Wolf and bear are wild! But my cow neighbors are domestic!
dialog.garden_animl3_0: Fish in water, birds in the sky — everyone has their own home!
dialog.garden_animl3_1: Cats walk on four legs! And birds fly!
dialog.garden_seasl1_0: Autumn is here — leaves are falling! Then winter will come!
dialog.garden_seasl1_1: There are four seasons in a year. Each one is special!
dialog.garden_seasl2_0: Spring! Snow melts, birds return! Everything blooms!
dialog.garden_seasl2_1: In spring I wake up from winter sleep! How wonderful!
dialog.garden_seasl3_0: Summer! Sunny and warm! You can swim!
dialog.garden_seasl3_1: After summer comes autumn again. The circle of nature!
dialog.island_abcl1_0: Squawk! Welcome to English Island! I'm Pete!
dialog.island_abcl1_1: The English alphabet has 26 letters! Let's start with A and B!
dialog.island_abcl2_0: Great! Now let's learn C and D!
dialog.island_abcl2_1: C is for Coconut! D is for Dolphin! Squawk!
dialog.island_abcl3_0: E is for Egg! F is for Frog!
dialog.island_abcl3_1: You know 6 letters: A, B, C, D, E, F! Magnificent!
dialog.island_coll1_0: Look at all the colors! Red, Blue, Green!
dialog.island_coll1_1: Colors describe the world! Let's learn them in English!
dialog.island_coll2_0: Yellow sun! Orange fruit! Can you see them?
dialog.island_coll2_1: Yellow bananas are my favorite! Squawk!
dialog.island_coll3_0: White snow! Black night! So many colors!
dialog.island_coll3_1: Wonderful! You know all the basic colors in English!
dialog.island_animl1_0: CAT! DOG! These are my island friends! Squawk!
dialog.island_animl1_1: In English: cat = кот, dog = собака! Easy!
dialog.island_animl2_0: BIRD can fly! FISH can swim!
dialog.island_animl2_1: I'm a bird! I can fly AND talk! Squawk!
dialog.island_animl3_0: COW says Moo! We learned cat, dog, bird, fish, cow!
dialog.island_animl3_1: You know 5 animal words in English! Amazing!
dialog.g3e_dailyl1_0: Hello! Today we are talking about the daily routine.
dialog.g3e_dailyl1_1: Tell me what you do every day!
dialog.g3e_dailyl2_0: Great! Now let's talk about time.
dialog.g3e_dailyl2_1: What time do you get up?
dialog.g3e_dailyl3_0: Super! Let's make up a story about your day.
dialog.g3e_dailyl3_1: Tell me in English what you do in the morning!
dialog.g1m_c20l1_0: Hi! I am Leo from Number City! Let us count to 20!
dialog.g1m_c20l1_1: Great! Numbers 11-20 are what you get when you add more to ten!
dialog.g1m_c20l2_0: Well done! Now numbers 16-20. They come in a row!
dialog.g1m_c20l2_1: Correct! 17 is between 16 and 18. You are already an expert!
dialog.g1m_c20l3_0: Comparing numbers! Which is bigger: 14 or 17?
dialog.g1m_c20l3_1: 17 is bigger than 14! You are doing great!
dialog.g1m_addl1_1: Count on your fingers or in your head. Try it!
dialog.g1m_addl2_0: Up to ten! How much do you need to add to 7 to get 10?
dialog.g1m_addl3_1: 10 + 5 = 15! You are already counting like a pro!
dialog.g1m_subl1_0: Subtraction — we take away a part. 7 - 3 =?
dialog.g1m_subl1_1: Imagine 7 apples. 3 were eaten. How many are left?
dialog.g1m_subl3_1: First add, then subtract. You can do it!
dialog.g1r_vowl1_0: Hello! I am Masha! Letters А, О, У are vowels!
dialog.g1r_vowl1_1: Vowels can be sung: А-А-А! In the word UTKA the first letter is U!
dialog.g1r_vowl2_0: Letters Я, Ю, Е, Ё are also vowels! They soften consonants.
dialog.g1r_vowl2_1: In the word ЮЛА the first letter is Ю! Remember it!
dialog.g1r_vowl3_0: Softness of consonants! КОН is hard, but in КОНЬ it is soft!
dialog.g1r_vowl3_1: The letter Ь shows softness. НОС is hard, НОЛЬ is soft!
dialog.g1r_wrdl1_0: Reading words! К-О-Т — КОТ. By syllables!
dialog.g1r_wrdl1_1: СОМ — one syllable. ДОМ — one syllable. Read!
dialog.g1r_wrdl2_0: The words СТОЛ and СТУЛ are similar. Read carefully!
dialog.g1r_wrdl2_1: ТРА-ВА — two syllables. КНИ-ГА — two syllables!
dialog.g1r_wrdl3_0: Reading sentences! Who? What does it do?
dialog.g1r_wrdl3_1: A sentence has a subject and a predicate. Look for them!
dialog.g1r_grml1_0: Capital letter! Names and the start of a sentence are written with a capital.
dialog.g1r_grml1_1: Маша, Москва, Тали — with a capital!
dialog.g1r_grml2_0: Punctuation! A full stop goes at the end of a sentence, a question mark in a question.
dialog.g1r_grml2_1: Who is this? — question. Mum is home. — statement.
dialog.g1r_grml3_0: Questions WHO? and WHAT? Who is running? What is growing?
dialog.g1r_grml3_1: WHO — about people and animals. WHAT — about objects!
dialog.g1w_schl1_0: Hello! I am Kesha! School supplies — pen, notebook, textbook!
dialog.g1w_schl1_1: At school we learn. In the classroom — desks and a board!
dialog.g1w_schl2_0: There are different lessons: maths, reading, PE!
dialog.g1w_schl2_1: In PE we run, in art we draw!
dialog.g1w_schl3_0: School is where we gain knowledge!
dialog.g1w_schl3_1: You already know a lot! Keep it up!
dialog.g1w_natl1_0: Trees — oak, birch, spruce. They have a trunk and leaves!
dialog.g1w_natl1_1: Animals live in the forest: hare, fox, bear!
dialog.g1w_natl2_0: Weather comes in many kinds: sun, rain, snow!
dialog.g1w_natl2_1: In autumn leaves turn yellow, in winter snow falls!
dialog.g1w_natl3_0: Nature is all around us! Take care of it!
dialog.g1w_natl3_1: Do not litter, do not break trees. We are part of nature!
dialog.g1w_bdyl1_0: Senses: eyes see, ears hear, nose smells!
dialog.g1w_bdyl1_1: Hands touch, tongue tastes. All are important!
dialog.g1w_bdyl2_0: Health is sport, exercise, healthy eating!
dialog.g1w_bdyl2_1: Fruit and vegetables are good for you. Sweets — in moderation!
dialog.g1w_bdyl3_0: Safety: do not talk to strangers!
dialog.g1w_bdyl3_1: Cross the road on green. Be careful!
dialog.g1e_abcl1_0: Hello! I am Polly! Letters G, H, I, J — learning more!
dialog.g1e_abcl1_1: G — giraffe, H — house. Let's continue!
dialog.g1e_abcl2_0: Letters K, L, M, N — the next in the alphabet!
dialog.g1e_abcl3_0: Letters O, P, Q, R — almost half the alphabet!
dialog.g1e_abcl3_1: O — orange, P — parrot. Well done!
dialog.g1e_numl1_0: Numbers in English: one, two, three, four, five!
dialog.g1e_numl2_0: Numbers 6-10: six, seven, eight, nine, ten!
dialog.g1e_numl3_0: Simple examples in English! Two plus three?
dialog.g1e_grtl2_1: Goodbye — until we meet again! Bye — bye!
dialog.g1e_grtl3_0: Thank you and Please are two very important polite phrases!
dialog.g1e_grtl3_1: Polite words are important in any language!
dialog.g2m_100l1_0: Hello! I am eagle Archi! Numbers up to 100 — tens!
dialog.g2m_100l1_1: 10, 20, 30... These are tens. Count in tens!
dialog.g2m_100l2_0: Place values: units and tens. 25 = 2 tens and 5 units!
dialog.g2m_100l2_1: Correct! The number 47 is 4 tens and 7 units!
dialog.g2m_100l3_0: Numbers up to 100! Comparing and counting!
dialog.g2m_100l3_1: 99 is the largest two-digit number! Well done!
dialog.g2m_add2l1_1: 20 + 30 = 50! Easy when you know the tens!
dialog.g2m_add2l3_1: 37 + 48 = 85! Units with units, tens with tens!
dialog.g2m_timesl2_1: Multiplying by 5 is easy — it ends in 0 or 5!
dialog.g2r_shl1_0: Hard consonants: Л, Р, М before А, О, У!
dialog.g2r_shl1_1: ЛА, ЛО, ЛУ — hard. ЛИ, ЛЕ — soft!
dialog.g2r_shl2_0: Soft sign Ь! Конь, соль, мать — softness at the end!
dialog.g2r_shl2_1: Ь does not represent a sound but makes the consonant soft!
dialog.g2r_shl3_0: Ль, Лю, Ле, Ла — the letter Л can be soft!
dialog.g2r_shl3_1: Любовь, лимон, лев — Л is soft!
dialog.g2r_spl1_0: Noun — who? what? Table, mum, sun!
dialog.g2r_spl1_1: A noun names an object or person!
dialog.g2r_spl2_0: Verb — what does it do? Runs, reads, sleeps!
dialog.g2r_spl2_1: A verb is an action. What does the cat do? It meows!
dialog.g2r_spl3_0: Adjective — what kind? Red, big, cheerful!
dialog.g2r_spl3_1: An adjective describes an object. Red ball!
dialog.g2r_sentl1_0: Subject and predicate — the main sentence members!
dialog.g2r_sentl1_1: Who? What? — subject. What does it do? — predicate!
dialog.g2r_sentl2_1: They clarify the main members of the sentence!
dialog.g2r_sentl3_0: Word connections in a sentence. Agreement!
dialog.g2r_sentl3_1: An adjective agrees with the noun in gender!
dialog.g2s_pltl1_0: Parts of a plant: root, stem, leaves, flower!
dialog.g2s_pltl1_1: Root is in the soil, leaves reach towards the sun!
dialog.g2s_pltl2_0: Photosynthesis — a plant breathes and feeds using sunlight!
dialog.g2s_pltl2_1: Leaves absorb light and make nutrients!
dialog.g2s_pltl3_0: Vegetables and fruit — the fruits of plants!
dialog.g2s_pltl3_1: Carrot is a root vegetable, apple is a fruit!
dialog.g2s_anil1_0: Mammals — feed their young with milk!
dialog.g2s_anil3_0: Fish live in water and breathe with gills!
dialog.g2s_bdyl1_0: Skeleton and muscles — the body's support!
dialog.g2s_bdyl1_1: Bones protect organs. Muscles help us move!
dialog.g2s_bdyl2_1: Every organ has its own job!
dialog.g2s_bdyl3_0: Eating well and doing sport — keys to health!
dialog.g2e_daysl1_0: Days of the week: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday...
dialog.g2e_daysl1_1: Monday is the first day of the week. There are seven days in a week!
dialog.g2e_daysl2_0: Yesterday is the day before today. Tomorrow is the day after today!
dialog.g2e_daysl2_1: Today is Monday. Yesterday was Sunday!
dialog.g2e_daysl3_0: Timetable: What day is it today?
dialog.g2e_daysl3_1: On Monday we have math. Weekly timetable!
dialog.g2e_phrl1_0: Please is a polite request. Thank you shows gratitude!
dialog.g2e_phrl2_0: Excuse me — sorry! Sorry — I apologise!
dialog.g2e_phrl2_1: When you are in the way — Excuse me. When you are at fault — Sorry!
dialog.g2e_phrl3_0: Can I? — May I? You can't — No, you can't!
dialog.g2e_phrl3_1: Ask for permission: Can I go?
dialog.g2e_schl1_0: In the classroom: desk, chair, board, book!
dialog.g2e_schl3_0: School phrases: May I come in? I don't understand.
dialog.g2e_schl3_1: Can you help me? — Can you help me?
dialog.g3m_tabl1_0: Times tables for 4 and 6! 4 x 5 = 20, 6 x 7 = 42!
dialog.g3m_tabl1_1: Multiplying by 4 — double and double again!
dialog.g3m_tabl2_0: Times tables for 7 and 8! Harder, but you can do it!
dialog.g3m_tabl3_0: Times table for 9! Finger trick: 9 x 6 = 54!
dialog.g3m_tabl3_1: The digits of any multiple of 9 always add up to 9! 9 x 5 = 45!
dialog.g3m_divl1_0: Division is the opposite of multiplication! 6 / 2 = 3 because 2 x 3 = 6!
dialog.g3m_divl3_0: The link between multiplication and division! 7 x 8 = 56, so 56 / 7 = 8!
dialog.g3r_genl1_0: Masculine and feminine gender! Table — he, book — she!
dialog.g3r_genl1_1: The gender of a noun determines the adjective ending!
dialog.g3r_genl2_0: Neuter gender: window, sea, happiness — it!
dialog.g3r_genl3_0: Gender of adjectives: big table, big book, big window!
dialog.g3r_genl3_1: An adjective agrees with the noun in gender!
dialog.g3r_verbl1_0: Verb in present tense: I read, you read!
dialog.g3r_verbl1_1: Endings change by person and number!
dialog.g3r_verbl3_0: Person of the verb: 1st (I, we), 2nd (you), 3rd (he, she, it, they)!
dialog.g3r_verbl3_1: I go — 1st person. He goes — 3rd person!
dialog.g3r_adjl1_1: Red ball, red rose, red apple!
dialog.g3r_adjl2_0: Degrees of comparison: big — bigger — biggest!
dialog.g3w_geol1_0: Cardinal directions: north, south, east, west!
dialog.g3w_geol2_0: Map and globe — a model of the Earth!
dialog.g3w_geol2_1: Countries and oceans are on the map!
dialog.g3w_geol3_0: Countries and capitals! Russia — Moscow, France — Paris!
dialog.g3w_natl1_0: The water cycle: evaporation, clouds, rain!
dialog.g3w_natl2_1: They are extracted from the ground!
dialog.g3w_ecol1_0: An ecosystem is a community of living organisms!
dialog.g3w_ecol3_0: People and nature. We are part of the ecosystem!
dialog.g3e_tobel1_0: The verb to be: I am, you are, he/she/it is!
dialog.g3e_tobel1_1: Am with I, is with he/she/it, are with you/we/they!
dialog.g3e_tobel2_0: Negation: I am not, he is not, they are not!
dialog.g3e_tobel2_1: Not goes after am, is, are!
dialog.g3e_tobel3_0: Questions: Am I? Is he? Are you?
dialog.g3e_tobel3_1: Am, is, are go at the start of a question!
dialog.g3e_foodl1_0: Food and drinks: apple, bread, milk, water!
dialog.g3e_foodl2_0: I like / I don't like — мага жагат / мага жакпайт!
dialog.g3e_foodl2_1: I like pizza. I do not like broccoli!
dialog.g3e_foodl3_0: At the table: Can I have some water? Thank you!
dialog.g3e_routel1_0: Daily routine: I get up, I brush my teeth!
dialog.g3e_routel1_1: Wake up — ойгонуу. Go to bed — уктоого баруу!
dialog.g3e_routel2_0: Time: What time is it? It's 7 o'clock!
dialog.g3e_routel2_1: O'clock — for a full hour. Half past — half!
dialog.g3e_routel3_1: I always brush my teeth. I never skip breakfast!
dialog.g4m_md_l1_0: Hi! I just found an old treasure map. It says: “The treasure is buried 3 475 steps from the oak.” I’ve already walked three thousand steps and I can’t tell — how far is left? Help me figure out big numbers!
dialog.g4m_md_l1_1: Tali, don’t worry. Big numbers are like a layered cake: first thousands, then hundreds, then tens, then ones. Let’s show Tali together!
dialog.g4m_md_l2_0: Digit, I need help! I wrote down the treasure safe number: 6 253. But I forgot what each digit means. If I enter it wrong — the safe won’t open!
dialog.g4m_md_l2_1: Easy, Tali. Place values are like a keyhole: each digit has its own spot and its own job. Let’s help Tali open the safe together!
dialog.g4m_md_l3_0: I found two treasures! The first has 8 450 coins, the second — 8 540. I want the bigger one, but I can’t decide — they look so alike!
dialog.g4m_md_l3_1: Tali, comparing numbers is like a race: you look at thousands first, then hundreds, and so on. The first one that “runs ahead” is the bigger number!
dialog.g4m_cm_l1_0: Digit, I opened a bakery for dinosaurs! Today I baked 213 buns. Tomorrow — the same, and the day after too. But I don’t know how many that makes in three days. Multiplying in columns feels too scary!
dialog.g4m_cm_l1_1: Tali, let me show you a trick: multiply each place separately, from the bottom up. It’s like stacking floors of a house — one by one, and it’s not scary!
dialog.g4m_cm_l2_0: The dinosaur building crew lays 1 346 bricks a day. I need to order bricks for 5 days, but the numbers are so big… Digit, I’m scared I’ll mess up and order too few!
dialog.g4m_cm_l2_1: Tali, for big numbers the column method is your best friend. Multiply each place and don’t forget to carry. Let’s go together!
dialog.g4m_cm_l3_0: This is really scary — multiplying a big number by a big number! 236 × 12… I don’t even know where to start. Digit, are you sure I can do this?
dialog.g4m_cm_l3_1: Tali, the main secret: multiply by the ones first, then by the tens — and shift the second result one step to the left. Two lines, then add. You’ve got this — I believe in you!
dialog.g4m_fr_l1_0: Digit, I have a problem! I cut a pizza for the party into 4 pieces. I ate one. How do I write how much I ate? A whole pizza — no, but zero — also no…
dialog.g4m_fr_l1_1: Tali, you just discovered fractions! “One part out of four” is the fraction 1/4. The numerator is how many you took, the denominator is how many equal parts you cut!
dialog.g4m_fr_l2_0: Digit, I’m cutting an apple into 4 parts. But… one piece came out bigger than the others. Is that still the fraction 1/4?
dialog.g4m_fr_l2_1: No, Tali! That’s the most important rule of fractions: the parts must be EQUAL. Otherwise the fraction just doesn’t work. Let’s cut it again — carefully!
dialog.g4m_fr_l3_0: My friend and I shared a pizza: I took 3/8, he took 5/8. He says he has more. I don’t believe it — the numbers look the same, only 3 and 5 are different!
dialog.g4m_fr_l3_1: Tali, you almost cracked the rule! When the denominators are the same — just look at the numerators: whoever has the bigger numerator has the bigger fraction. It’s like a contest!
dialog.g4r_conj_l1_0: Hi, I’m Word! Today Tali wrote in his diary: “Я хожу в школу. Ты ходишь в школу. Он ходить в школу.” Something’s wrong in the third sentence — Tali didn’t notice the mistake!
dialog.g4r_conj_l1_1: Really? I thought everything was fine… Please explain!
dialog.g4r_conj_l2_0: Word, I’m writing a play about dinosaurs! There’s a line like this: “Мы петь вместе!” Sounds beautiful, right?
dialog.g4r_conj_l2_1: Tali, “мы петь” isn’t conjugation! You need to change the verb by person. “Мы поём” — that’s how it should sound. Let’s fix the play together!
dialog.g4r_conj_l3_0: Word, I’m almost done with the play! But the last line won’t come out: “Мы бежит к финишу!” Something sounds off…
dialog.g4r_conj_l3_1: Tali, you can feel the mistake — that’s a good sign! Now we need to find the verb’s conjugation and pick the right ending. You already know almost everything!
dialog.g4r_cases_l1_0: Word, I’m lost in cases! “Кот лежит” and “Я вижу кота” — why is it «кот» in one place and «кота» in the other?
dialog.g4r_cases_l1_1: Tali, those are two different cases! Nominative answers “кто?” — it’s the subject, the owner of the sentence. Accusative — “кого? что?” — is the object of the action. Let’s figure it out!
dialog.g4r_cases_l2_0: Word, I need to write a letter to a friend! “Я отправил письмо мама” — is that right? Something sounds weird…
dialog.g4r_cases_l2_1: Tali, you can feel it — «мама» doesn’t fit here! After “отправил кому?” you need dative: «маме». And “не хватает кого?” — genitive: «мамы». Let’s look at both!
dialog.g4r_cases_l3_0: Word, the last two cases! Instrumental and prepositional — the most mysterious names. Is “instrumental” because you create something?
dialog.g4r_cases_l3_1: You almost guessed, Tali! Instrumental is “creating with the help of something.” “Пишу карандашом” — instrumental. And prepositional — because it is always used WITH a preposition. Never without one!
dialog.g4r_text_l1_0: Word, I read the story “Солнце зашло. Стало темно. Птицы умолкли.” It’s very short. What’s it even about? I don’t get it!
dialog.g4r_text_l1_1: Tali, even a short text has a topic! These three sentences together paint a picture. Close your eyes — what do you see? That’s the topic!
dialog.g4r_text_l2_0: I read a text about a hedgehog: “Ёж свернулся в клубок. Иголки торчат во все стороны. Никто не тронет ежа.” Word, what’s the main idea here? There are three sentences — and each one matters!
dialog.g4r_text_l2_1: Tali, the main idea isn’t one of the sentences — it’s what the author wanted to say with the whole text. Why was this text written? What should the reader understand?
dialog.g4r_text_l3_0: Word, I read about Masha looking for mushrooms. “Потом позвала сестру. Наконец набрали корзину. Сначала нашла гриб.” Something’s wrong with the order — my head is spinning!
dialog.g4r_text_l3_1: Tali, the order of events in a text is sequence! Words like “сначала”, “потом”, “наконец” are beacons that show what comes after what. Let’s put the order back!
dialog.g4e_pres_l1_0: Hi! I’m Spark — Tali’s new friend on English Island! Tali just wrote in English: “She go to school every day.” I can tell something’s wrong — but I can’t explain why!
dialog.g4e_pres_l1_1: I tried my best! Isn’t “go” okay?
dialog.g4e_pres_l2_0: Spark, I need to say that the cat doesn’t eat fish. I wrote: “The cat not eats fish.” Is that right?
dialog.g4e_pres_l2_1: Tali, almost! In Present Simple, negation uses don’t or doesn’t — not just “not.” With he/she/it — doesn’t, with the others — don’t. Shall we try again?
dialog.g4e_pres_l3_0: Spark, how do I ask in English: “Does she speak French?” I wrote: “She speak French?” It sounds a bit short…
dialog.g4e_pres_l3_1: Tali, for a question we need a helping verb — Does! It “jumps” to the front. “Does she speak French?” Let’s try!
dialog.g4e_past_l1_0: Spark, yesterday I climbed a mountain. How do I say that in English? “Yesterday we climb the mountain.”
dialog.g4e_past_l1_1: Tali, that’s the past tense — Past Simple! Regular verbs get the ending -ed. “We climbed” — that’s how!
dialog.g4e_past_l2_0: Spark, I wrote in my diary: “Last night I haved a strange dream.” Is that right?
dialog.g4e_past_l2_1: Tali, “have” is an irregular verb! It has a special past form — “had.” These verbs you learn by heart; they don’t add -ed!
dialog.g4e_past_l3_0: Spark, I’m writing a story about Anna: “Last Saturday, Anna meet her friends and they watch a film.” Is that right?
dialog.g4e_past_l3_1: Tali, two verbs — and both in the wrong form! Meet is irregular, watch is regular. Let’s fix them together — and your story will be great!
dialog.g4e_quest_l1_0: Spark, I want to ask you: do you like ice cream? I wrote: “You like ice cream?” Is that right?
dialog.g4e_quest_l1_1: Tali, you’re missing the helping verb! “Do you like ice cream?” — that’s a question you can answer with “Yes” or “No.” We’ll have lots of those today!
dialog.g4e_quest_l2_0: Spark, I lost my hat! How do I ask where it is? I wrote “What is my hat?” — but that’s not about place…
dialog.g4e_quest_l2_1: Tali, “What” means “what,” but you need “where” — that’s “Where”! Question words are like keys: each opens its own lock. Let’s look at them all!
dialog.g4e_quest_l3_0: Spark, you asked: “Do you like cats?” I answered: “Yes, I likes.” Is that right?
dialog.g4e_quest_l3_1: Tali, in a short answer we repeat the helping verb — do or does, did! “Yes, I do.” Short, clear, correct!
dialog.g4s_help_l1_0: Hi! I’m Friendly — your guide in the City of Social Skills. Today Tali is trying to open a heavy door with bags in his paws — and he just can’t. He’s been standing there five minutes and turning red. What does he need to do?
dialog.g4s_help_l1_1: I don’t want to ask for help — it’s awkward…
dialog.g4s_help_l2_0: Friendly, I need an eraser from the kid next to me. I said: “Give me the eraser!” He gave it, but looked kind of grumpy… Why?
dialog.g4s_help_l2_1: Tali, “Give me the eraser” is an order, not a request! The word “please” and a friendly tone turn a demand into an invitation to cooperate. Shall we try another way?
dialog.g4s_help_l3_0: Friendly, today I had three situations where I needed help. I didn’t know how to handle each one… Walk through them with me?
dialog.g4s_help_l3_1: Of course! Looking at real situations is the best way to learn. Let’s go!
dialog.g4s_emo_l1_0: Friendly, today my friend came to school with slumped shoulders and a quiet voice. I didn’t know what to say… Is that sadness?
dialog.g4s_emo_l1_1: Tali, you already know how to read emotions from outer signs — that’s an important skill! Slumped shoulders, a quiet voice — yes, those are signs of sadness. Let’s look at how to respond well.
dialog.g4s_emo_l2_0: Friendly, my brother broke my dinosaur model! I’m so angry I want to throw something. How do I deal with this?
dialog.g4s_emo_l2_1: Tali, anger is a normal emotion! But it’s important to show it safely. Tell your brother in words how much it hurts — that’s much better than throwing things.
dialog.g4s_emo_l3_0: Friendly, I walked into class and saw a surprise on my desk! My eyes went wide, my mouth opened a little… What was that?
dialog.g4s_emo_l3_1: Tali, that’s surprise! It can be pleasant (like your surprise) or unpleasant. And calm is the opposite: even breathing, relaxed shoulders, thoughts without panic.
dialog.g4s_turn_l1_0: Friendly, there’s a long line in the cafeteria. A friend waves from the middle of the line and calls me forward. Everyone’s looking…
dialog.g4s_turn_l1_1: Tali, this is a tricky moment! Your friend wants to help, but cutting the line hurts the rights of people who are waiting. Respect for the line is respect for people. What should you do?
dialog.g4s_turn_l2_0: Friendly, three of my friends all want to ride my scooter at the same time. I don’t know how to share fairly — someone will get upset!
dialog.g4s_turn_l2_1: Tali, fairness isn’t always “exactly equal” — it’s when everyone understands the rules and agrees with them. Let’s invent a solution together!
dialog.g4s_turn_l3_0: Friendly, during a board game I noticed one player peeking at the cards! What should I do — yell or stay quiet?
dialog.g4s_turn_l3_1: Tali, game rules are an agreement between everyone playing. Breaking the rules is called unfair play. You don’t need to yell — calmly name the problem and suggest a fix.
dialog.g2e_phrl3_2: No, you can't — this is MY sandwich, Tali!
dialog.g2s_anil2_2: Hmm… that’s a good question. Honestly, I’m a little unsure…
